paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Distribution of articles across media outlets
model_annotation: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of articles across various media outlets. The chart is divided into 21 segments, each representing a different media source. The largest segment, colored gray, represents "Other" and accounts for approximately 14% of the articles. Following this is Breitbart, shown in teal, with 13%. The remaining slices consist of "The Guardian" (brown, 13%), CNN (light gray, 14%), Fox News (orange, 3%), PoliticusUSA (dark red, 3%), Shareblue (light blue, 3%), Daily Kos (dark blue, 3%), National Review (purple, 3%), Daily Caller (light green, 8%), The Huffington Post (forest green, 8%), Drudge Report (dark green, 8%), NPR (violet, 7%), Vox (pink, 6%), The Daily Mail (light yellow, 5%), BBC (yellow, 5%), RT (sky blue, 3%), and smaller segments representing "Red State" (tan, 3%), and "National Review" (purple, 3%). The visual arrangement places slices in a roughly descending order by size, although there are some exceptions. Percentage labels are displayed within each slice, and there is no legend included, nor are any slices visually emphasized through exploding or bolding.
